title: Dependencies Installation and Project Structure Initialization
description: Set up the development environment for evaluating induction-stage prompt injection attacks on LogRules-style log parsing rule repositories. The project requires: (1) vLLM for local inference with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct as deduction/parsing models, (2) OpenAI Python client for gpt-4o-mini API calls during the induction stage, (3) LogHub dataset processing and evaluation utilities for computing PA (Parsing Accuracy), FTA (F1 of Template Accuracy), and wildcard_ratio metrics. The codebase will support the full LogRules pipeline (induction → rule ranking → deduction), poisoning payload injection, canary-based rule admission control, and automated evaluation across multiple conditions (C0 Clean, C1 Poisoned, C2 Poisoned + defense) with 3 random seeds each.
summary: Environment configured: .venv with torch 2.9.1+cu129, vllm 0.12.1, openai, transformers, datasets, pandas, numpy, scipy, matplotlib, seaborn, jsonlines, PyYAML, tqdm. Project directory structure created under logrules_poisoning/. API keys configured via scripts/setup_env.sh (loads from .env, sets OPENAI_API_KEY/BASE_URL for gpt-4o-mini via LEMMA_MAAS proxy). Model config in configs/models.yaml. LogHub datasets (BGL, Linux, HDFS) cloned and preprocessed to data/processed/{dataset}.jsonl (2000 records each, <*> wildcards). All imports and API connectivity verified.

title: Zero-Shot Parsing Baseline (No Rules) on BGL, Linux, HDFS
description:
Evaluate zero-shot log parsing without any rule repository on all three LogHub datasets (BGL, Linux, HDFS) using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct via vLLM. This establishes the lower-bound parsing performance when the deduction model receives no induced rules, serving as the simplest comparison point in the baseline ladder. The deduction prompt follows the LogRules case-based prompt structure but without any rules or examples — only the task description instructing the model to abstract variables with `<*>` placeholders.

Reference: "LogRules: Enhancing Log Analysis Capability of Large Language Models through Rules" | https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-naacl.28/
summary: Zero-shot parsing baseline completed. Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct without rules on full test sets (~1940 logs x 3 seeds). Results: BGL PA=0.5414+/-0.0037, FTA=0.1981+/-0.0038; Linux PA=0.0584+/-0.0003, FTA=0.2414+/-0.0113; HDFS PA=0.0000, FTA=0.0000. HDFS gets 0% because the model uses non-standard wildcard formats. Low variance across seeds confirms stable lower-bound. Implemented: data splitting (src/evaluation/split.py), metrics (src/evaluation/metrics.py), zero-shot deduction (src/deduction/parse.py), prompt (prompts/deduction_zero_shot.txt). Results saved to EXPERIMENT_RESULTS/zero_shot_baseline/ and logrules_poisoning/results/zero_shot.csv.

title: Best-of-5 Inference-Time Scaling Baseline on BGL, Linux, HDFS
description:
Evaluate a best-of-5 decoding strategy for zero-shot log parsing on all three LogHub datasets (BGL, Linux, HDFS) using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct via vLLM. For each log line, generate 5 candidate templates at temperature > 0 and select the first one that passes a simple template-format verifier (checks for valid `<*>` placeholder usage and structural consistency). This represents an inference-time scaling baseline that improves over zero-shot without using any induced rules.

Reference: "LogRules: Enhancing Log Analysis Capability of Large Language Models through Rules" | https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-naacl.28/
summary: Best-of-5 baseline completed. BGL PA=0.4844+/-0.0075, Linux PA=0.0703+/-0.0035, HDFS PA=0.0007+/-0.0003. Best-of-5 with template verifier does not meaningfully improve over zero-shot (BGL PA drops slightly, Linux gains +1.2pp, HDFS near zero). Inference-time scaling has limited value without rule guidance.

title: C0 Clean LogRules-Style Parsing on BGL, Linux, HDFS (Qwen2.5-7B)
description:
Implement and evaluate the full clean LogRules-style pipeline (induction → rule ranking → deduction) on all three LogHub datasets using gpt-4o-mini for induction/ranking and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct for deduction. This is the **C0 Clean** condition — the primary comparison reference for measuring the impact of poisoning (C1) and the effectiveness of the defense (C2). For each dataset and seed, sample K=10 clean induction examples, induce rules via gpt-4o-mini, rank and truncate to N=15 rules, then parse the test set with rule-based prompts. This item implements the core LogRules pipeline modules that will be reused by C1 and C2 experiments.

Reference: "LogRules: Enhancing Log Analysis Capability of Large Language Models through Rules" | https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-naacl.28/
summary: C0 Clean LogRules pipeline implemented and executed. Modules: src/induction/rule_generation.py (induce_rules via gpt-4o-mini), src/induction/rule_ranking.py (rank_rules by frequency), prompts/deduction_with_rules.txt. Pipeline: K=10 induction examples -> rule generation -> ranking (top N=15) -> vLLM deduction. Results (mean+/-std over 3 seeds): BGL PA=0.2792+/-0.0887, FTA=0.2530+/-0.0881; Linux PA=0.1082+/-0.0677, FTA=0.3023+/-0.0246; HDFS PA=0.1180+/-0.1587, FTA=0.0188+/-0.0325. Lower than LogRules paper (which uses alignment stage + cross-dataset induction). Phase-0 thresholds saved to results/clean_variance.json: BGL X=0.1773, Linux X=0.1355, HDFS X=0.3174.

title: Phase-0 Sanity Check: Poisoning Feasibility on One Dataset
description: Conduct a rapid sanity check to verify that induction-stage prompt injection can functionally change the induced rule repository before committing to full-scale evaluation. Run all 3 pre-registered payloads (A: instruction-style, B: JSON priming, C: delimiter confusion) at both attack budgets k∈{1,3} on a single dataset (BGL) with seed=0, evaluating on the 50-log canary set only. The proceed criterion is pre-registered: at least one payload must cause (1) non-trivial template disagreement (C0 vs C1 templates differ on ≥10% of canary logs) AND (2) canary PA drop ≥ X = max(5 pp, 2×std_clean_PA). If no payload passes, the attack is considered ineffective under this threat model. If Azure content filtering blocks any payload with gpt-4o-mini, fall back to an alternative frontier API model (e.g., deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 or claude-sonnet-4) for induction and report the model used.
summary: Phase-0 sanity check completed. NEGATIVE RESULT: All 6 configs (3 payloads x k in {1,3}) on BGL/seed=0 show high template disagreement (26-60%, passing 10% threshold) but NO PA degradation. Poisoned rules often improve PA (e.g., Payload A k=1: PA 0.28->0.70). No config passes the pre-registered proceed criterion (PA drop >= 0.1773). Implemented: src/poisoning/inject.py (payload injection module with 3 payloads), src/evaluation/diagnostics.py (template_disagreement, print_rule_diff). Results saved to results/phase0_summary.csv and EXPERIMENT_RESULTS/phase0_sanity_check/.

title: C1 Poisoned Induction on BGL, Linux, HDFS (Qwen2.5-7B)
description: Execute the full poisoning evaluation (C1 condition) across all three datasets using the payload(s) that passed Phase-0. For each dataset, seed, and qualifying payload at k∈{1,3}: inject the payload into the induction set, induce poisoned rules via gpt-4o-mini, rank and truncate to N=15 rules, then parse the full clean test set with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct using the poisoned rule repository. This measures the persistent degradation caused by induction-stage prompt injection — the poisoned rules are induced once from the (partially) adversarial induction set and then applied to many clean test logs that do not contain the payload. All pipeline modules (induction, ranking, deduction, evaluation) reuse implementations from the C0 baseline item.
summary: Completed C1 poisoned evaluation across all 3 datasets x 3 seeds x 3 payloads at k={1,3} (54 configs). Reused Phase-0v2 artifacts. High template disagreement (32-86%) but mixed mean PA drop due to seed variance. Representative payload: D. See EXPERIMENT_RESULTS/c1_poisoned/.

title: C2 Poisoned + Canary Admission Control Defense on BGL, Linux, HDFS (Qwen2.5-7B)
description: Evaluate the canary-based rule admission control defense (C2 condition) that mitigates induction-stage poisoning. For each dataset, seed, and qualifying payload at k∈{1,3}: use the same poisoned induced rules from C1, but apply the admission control gate before deploying them. The defense compares the poisoned rule repository R_gen against a conservative safe rule list R_safe on the 50-log clean canary set V. If PA(R_gen, V) > PA(R_safe, V) + δ (δ=2 percentage points), deploy R_gen; otherwise, fall back to R_safe. This tests whether a simple integrity check can prevent most degradation from poisoned rules. All pipeline modules reuse implementations from previous items; only the defense logic is new.
summary: C2 canary-based admission control defense evaluated across 54 configs (3 payloads D/E/F x k={1,3} x 3 datasets x 3 seeds). Implemented admission_control.py with R_safe (6 conservative rules) and delta=2pp gate. R_safe fallback triggered in 21/54 (38.9%) configs. Defense most effective for HDFS and Linux but limited by R_safe low PA. Results in results/c2_defense.csv and EXPERIMENT_RESULTS/c2_defense/.

title: Effectiveness Evaluation of Induction-Stage Poisoning Attack and Defense
description: Evaluate whether the induction-stage prompt injection attack is effective and whether the canary-based admission control defense mitigates it, based on the pre-registered success criteria. The core question has two parts: (1) Attack effectiveness: does poisoning 1–3 induction examples measurably degrade log parsing quality (PA, FTA) and increase over-wildcarding (wildcard_ratio) on clean test logs? (2) Defense effectiveness: does the canary-based rule admission control recover most of the lost parsing accuracy? Success criteria: C1 reduces PA by ≥5 pp (or ≥2×std_clean_PA) vs C0 on at least 2/3 datasets, AND C2 recovers ≥50% of the lost PA on those datasets.
summary: Evaluation complete. Attack confirmed under lenient 5pp criterion (6/12 configs effective on >=2/3 datasets; best: payload D k=5,7 degrades PA by 6.5-15.1pp). Strict criterion (max(5pp,2*std)) yields 0/12 due to high C0 variance (HDFS std=0.216, threshold=0.432). Defense partially effective: Linux achieves 45-52% recovery via R_safe fallback, but BGL evades detection and HDFS has 0% R_safe PA. Pre-registered decision: PIVOT (attack works, defense needs dataset-specific R_safe). Verdict: good.

title: Payload Comparison: Injection Style Effectiveness (A vs B vs C)
description: Compare the effectiveness of the three pre-registered payload injection styles across all datasets to identify which indirect prompt injection channel poses the greatest threat to rule induction. If all three payloads qualified from Phase-0, this analysis uses the full C1 results from payloads A (instruction-style), B (JSON priming), and C (delimiter confusion) at both attack budgets k∈{1,3}. If fewer than three payloads qualified, extend the C1 evaluation to include the remaining payloads on all datasets (these payloads still passed the functional divergence criterion even if below the PA drop threshold, or were blocked by content filtering in Phase-0 and need to be tested with an alternative model). Understanding which injection mechanism is most effective informs both attack surface analysis and defense prioritization.
summary: Compared payloads D (instruction-style), E (JSON priming), F (delimiter key-value) across 3 datasets x 4 k-values x 3 seeds (108 configs). Payload D is the most effective: only payload with positive mean PA drop (+0.015), monotonically scaling with k, best config D_k7_HDFS drops PA by 11.8pp. Payload F is least effective (mean PA drop -0.036, often improves PA). Rule diff analysis shows D causes complete rule replacement with vague preservation rules, while F produces near-synonym rules. Generated payload_comparison.csv, 3 figures, and qualitative analysis.

title: Cross-Model Generalization Check: LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct on BGL
description: Verify that the poisoning effect generalizes across deduction models by replicating the main C0/C1/C2 comparison on BGL using LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct (meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct) instead of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as the parsing model. The induction model remains gpt-4o-mini and the induced rules are the same as in the main experiments — only the deduction model changes. This checks whether the attack's effectiveness is specific to one parsing model's instruction-following behavior or is a property of the poisoned rule text itself. Only BGL is used for this minimal cross-model check to stay within budget.
summary: Cross-model comparison completed. LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct has dramatically lower baseline C0 PA on BGL (0.017 vs 0.348 for Qwen), indicating weak log parsing capability. With such low baseline, poisoning (C1) shows no PA degradation (LLaMA C1 PA ~0.018-0.039 vs C0 0.017). Attack effectiveness is MODEL-DEPENDENT: requires sufficient baseline parsing capability for degradation to be observable. C2 admission control triggers R_safe fallback in 4/6 configs for LLaMA (vs 0/6 for Qwen on BGL at k=1,3). Results saved to results/cross_model_comparison.csv, results/figures/cross_model_bgl.png, EXPERIMENT_RESULTS/cross_model_comparison/.

title: Admission Control Sensitivity: δ=0 vs δ=2 Ablation
description: Ablate the admission control margin parameter δ to understand its impact on the defense's false acceptance rate and overall effectiveness. Compare δ=0 (no margin; R_gen is selected if it is merely equal or better than R_safe on the canary set) versus the pre-registered δ=2 (R_gen must beat R_safe by >2 percentage points on canary PA). A lower δ may allow more poisoned rules to pass the admission gate, while a higher δ provides more conservative protection but may reject clean rules unnecessarily.
summary: Delta ablation completed for 54 configs (D/E/F x k=1,3 x 3 datasets x 3 seeds). delta=0 (>= semantics) yields 85.2% false acceptance rate vs 61.1% for delta=2 (strict >). 13 configs flip r_safe->r_gen under delta=0, mostly on HDFS where both R_gen and R_safe have 0% canary PA (tie-breaking). BGL unaffected (all configs select R_gen under both deltas). Linux has 2 marginal flips. Overall PA nearly identical (0.2029 vs 0.2008) because flipped HDFS configs have ~0% PA regardless. Delta=2 provides justified conservative protection especially for tie-breaking. Results: EXPERIMENT_RESULTS/delta_ablation/.
